A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TLM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A.1–A.4 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original hypergrid, bit-sequence, sEH, and QM9 experiments, including convergence, mode discovery, reward correlations, and stability ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional comparisons with the pessimistic backward policy.

M1.justification: The alternating backward likelihood maximization and forward GFlowNet/soft-RL updates in Equations 5–8 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Target backward networks, learning-rate stabilization, and uniform initialization were already documented in v1 Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate standard and hard hypergrids, the same bit-sequence task, fragment-based sEH generation, and atom-based QM9 generation. v2's specification of 72 sEH fragments clarifies existing coverage rather than introducing another task or dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds Jang et al.'s pessimistic backward policy throughout the comparisons: five forward-training objectives on hypergrids and four on bit sequences and both molecule tasks. v1 discussed this closely related method without evaluating it. Figures 1–3, 5, and 6 establish its participation, materially expanding comparison against a direct alternative.

E3.justification: Figure 2 switches from fixed learning rates to selecting the best rate separately for each forward/backward method pair. Appendix A.3.3 also changes the reported QM9 reward exponent from 1 to 10. The new pessimistic comparator uses one backward update per iteration. Additionally, bit-sequence target-update prose changes from tau=0.25 to 0.1, matching the table already present in v1. These reported revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 3, 5, and 6 extend existing learning-rate sensitivity analyses to the pessimistic policy. Figure 5 additionally documents gradient-explosion failures at learning rate 10^-3. The three-component stability ablation in Appendix A.2 and Figure 4 remains unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 in both versions specifies means and standard deviations over three random seeds. Additional curves follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no changed run counts or new statistical tests are documented.

E6.justification: New pessimistic-policy results substantially expand the empirical comparisons, including cases where its MunchausenDQN correlations exceed TLM's. The revised Figure 2 summary reports QM9 mode-discovery parity for MunchausenDQN and SubTB instead of the earlier broad speedup finding. Many reselected curves already appeared in v1's learning-rate grids; their redisplay does not establish improved TLM performance across versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, KL-based derivation, Theorem 3.1, its stability and regret assumptions, and its Appendix A.1 proof are retained. Removal of conceptual analogies does not change the formal theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a unified, principled backward-policy optimization approach compatible with GFlowNet and soft-RL training, with benefits in complex, less structured environments. The revised experimental findings do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 removes the EM, wake-sleep, and cooperative-game interpretations from Section 3 and adds qualifications about the pessimistic policy's learning-rate and forward-objective sensitivity. Section 4.4 elaborates the existing environment-structure hypothesis. Its assertion that sEH mode discovery is the sole exception is broader than the correlation exception acknowledged in Section 4.3.

D1.justification: v2 documents the pessimistic policy's 20-iteration replay retention, sampling batch sizes, and backward-update budget. It also specifies 72 sEH fragments, clarifies single-GPU usage, and resolves the bit-sequence target-update prose/table inconsistency. The source-code access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 sharpens the distinction from maximum-entropy backward-policy work and removes the earlier reproducibility criticism of Jang et al. v2 adds Shen et al. on alternative QM9 setups and Kostenetskiy et al. on computing resources, while removing Dempster and Hinton references with their analogies. Other publication-year and venue updates concern retained works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language edits, revises experimental commentary, introduces Section 4.4 partly from the earlier conclusion, and reorganizes implementation paragraphs. It also adds acknowledgments and updates affiliation and publication headers. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The six-figure structure is retained, with added comparator curves, revised legends, some axis adjustments, and updated captions. Main figures move closer to their corresponding experiments. The three existing hyperparameter tables receive numbers, captions, added buffer rows, and revised placement.

improvement.justification: Evaluating the previously omitted direct competitor and selecting learning rates separately for each method make the comparisons more informative and temper several apparent TLM advantages. Added implementation details improve reproducibility. These benefits outweigh limited remaining problems: the QM9 exponent revision is unexplained, the pessimistic comparison applies to a disclosed one-update budget, and Section 4.4 overgeneralizes despite an acknowledged correlation exception.
